title: Aromatic Chewy Ethiopian Lentils Kik Alicha
description: A wine‑enhanced, chewy lentil dish infused with miso and cornstarch, perfect for festive Ethiopian feasts.
instructions: Rinse 200g of red lentils under cold water until clear, then set aside.
In a 4‑quart pot, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat, then add 1 diced onion and 2 minced garlic cloves, sauté until translucent.
Stir in 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger and 1 teaspoon each of cumin and turmeric, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 1 cup of white wine, allowing it to reduce by half, then stir in 2 tablespoons of miso paste until dissolved.
Pour in 4 cups of low-sodium vegetable broth and the rinsed lentils; bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 25 minutes, uncovered.
In a small bowl, whisk 2 teaspoons of cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of broth to form a slurry, then slowly pour into the pot while stirring, cooking for an additional 5 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, and let the dish rest off‑heat for 5 minutes to set the texture.
Transfer the Kik Alicha to a lazy-susan-spinner, swirl to distribute evenly, and serve hot accompanied by injera or steamed rice.
